papers.title: Closure-guided Optimization: Minimum Structural Repair as a General Constraint-handling Principle
papers.authors: Mohammad Amir Khusru Akhtar
papers.abstract:
<jats:p><div>
 <div>
  <div>
   <div>
    <div>
     <div>
      <p>Constraint handling in population-based optimization is usually organized around violation magnitudes, feasibility rules, penalties, or repair operators, but these mechanisms do not treat the minimum admissible cost of reaching feasibility as the primitive search quantity. Building on Closure Complexity, this paper develops Closure-Guided Optimization (CGO) and Feasibility Closure Complexity (FCC), defined as the least admissible repair cost from a candidate to the feasible locus. We establish a universal repair lower bound, positive-rescaling invariance, an optimality criterion based on the repair ratio, and ranking stability for approximate FCC. The framework is evaluated across genetic algorithms, differential evolution, particle swarm optimization, a separable CMA-ES host, NSGA-II, and ant-colony optimization. Five experimental blocks examine controlled representation invariance; external constrained problems, including welded-beam engineering design; disconnected feasible regions with learned FCC; constrained multiobjective search; and exact interaction-aware set-cover repair, supplemented by an ACO discrete-host validation. Across 4,770 continuous optimization runs, 4,765 repair states, and 60 ACO runs, FCC is most useful when violation ranking diverges from repair difficulty, while normalized violation matches FCC when both encode the same geometry. Interaction-aware joint repair reaches a median cost ratio of 1.000 relative to exact FCC, with an 18.0% mean cost saving, whereas mixed NSGA-II results and the ACO null case show that FCC does not provide a universal advantage. These results support CGO as a conditional, measurable constraint-handling principle.<span></span></p>

papers.title: Why AI Adoption Fails: A Constraint-Based Diagnostic Model for Organizational Readiness
papers.authors: John Kwarsick
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence use has broadened quickly, but sustained organizational adoption remains uneven. McKinsey's 2025 global survey reports that 88 percent of respondents say their organizations use AI in at least one business function, yet nearly two-thirds remain in experimentation or piloting and only 39 percent report any enterprise-level EBIT impact from AI use (McKinsey &amp; Company, 2025). Gartner projected that at least 30 percent of generative AI projects would be abandoned after proof of concept by the end of 2025 (Gartner, 2024), while RAND notes estimates that more than 80 percent of AI projects fail (Ryseff et al., 2024). These patterns suggest that technical capability and organizational adoption are not the same problem. This paper proposes that many stalled AI initiatives are best understood as a constraint-diagnosis problem. Existing readiness, change-management, and adoption frameworks often describe broad conditions associated with implementation success, but they are less effective at identifying which single human or organizational factor is most limiting progress in a given system at a given moment. As a result, organizations frequently improve visible symptoms while the binding constraint remains untouched. To address that gap, this paper introduces THE WHEEL Framework™, a conceptual diagnostic architecture for organizational readiness. The framework integrates five established research traditions-theory of constraints, psychological safety, social identity, innovation diffusion, and trust in automation-and organizes readiness across eight dimensions: Identity, Psychological Safety, Workflow Integration, AI Environment, Social Dynamics, Leadership Signals, Learning Depth, and Measurement. Its central claim is that readiness is often asymmetric: one weak dimension can disproportionately limit adoption and distort the symptoms observed elsewhere. The paper contributes a constraint-based perspective to the AI adoption literature. It positions adoption failure not simply as a technology, training, or change-management problem, but as a socio-technical bottleneck problem shaped by identity, trust, workflow design, leadership behavior, learning systems, and feedback loops. The assessment instrument, item set, weighting logic, and scoring implementation are intentionally omitted. This publication is limited to the conceptual architecture and research argument.</jats:p>

papers.title: Autocatalytic Constraint Closure as an Organizational Principle for Machine Consciousness
papers.authors: Armando Vieira; Liane Gabora
papers.abstract:
<jats:p>Current AI systems are largely organized around prediction-error minimization and reward optimization. While these frameworks have been highly successful, they do
not address how AI systems can develop the kind of integrated, self-maintaining world-model widely regarded as central to consciousness. This paper proposes autocatalytic
constraint closure as a necessary organizational principle for machine consciousness. Reflexively Autocatalytic Foodset-derived (RAF) networks provide a general-purpose
formal framework for describing and analyzing the emergence of systems whose components catalyze the generation of new components that increase the coherence of the whole. This can result in a phase transition to a self-organizing system with history-dependent dynamics. Applied to cognition, external stimuli and internal representations ‘catalyze’ mental operations yielding new representations, spurring formation of an integrated representational network and coherent world-model. In this initial phase of research applying RAF networks to machine consciousness, we show that (i) AI systems instantiate limited, task-bound forms of autocatalytic organization but lack persistent closure across contexts, and (ii) in-context learning may be due to transient RAF formation. Next steps include fostering sensitivity to internal incoherence and question-asking in AI systems with the aim of fostering endogenously driven self-organization, a prerequisite for conscious systems, and the use of RAF algorithms to analyze candidates for machine consciousness.</jats:p>

papers.title: Constraint-Driven Database Repair
Aging as Cross-Hallmark Obstruction Amplification:A Sheaf-Theoretic Model of Repair Closure, Senescence, Inflammation, and Regenerative Failure
papers.authors: Juan Segura
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Aging is usually described as the accumulation of molecular, cellular, tissue, and systemic defects. The twelve-hallmark framework has made this description biologically precise, but it still leaves open a structural question: why do heterogeneous defects begin to behave as one organism-level loss of repair capacity? Aging is formalized as loss of autopoietic repair closure in a sheaf-theoretic model. The central claim is that aging is not the negation of life, but the narrowing of the space in which a living system can repair, regenerate, and preserve its own organization. Each hallmark is represented as a local-to-global constraint layer over a tissue, cellular, or organismal complex. Viable self-maintenance corresponds to global sections; unresolved incompatibilities correspond to cohomological obstructions; repair failure is tracked by persistence under injury, stress, or regeneration filtrations. The twelve hallmarks are coupled by an extension whose connecting morphism measures when coherent regulatory or interface states generate material-repair incompatibilities. The main formal result is an exact repair-reserve decomposition: organismal repair reserve equals material-repair closure plus regulatory-interface closure minus cross-hallmark obstruction rank. A categorical layer complements this result: by the Yoneda principle, aging is visible as deformation of the complete experimental response profile, while senescence is represented as an idempotent cellular retract. Further results show that cross-hallmark interactions amplify obstruction rank beyond isolated hallmark effects; aged systems can remain viable at baseline while losing repair closure under challenge; and local improvement of one hallmark is not equivalent to organismal rejuvenation unless it expands the benign repair-control kernel. A computable senescence--inflammation--stem-cell model illustrates the theory through rank regimes, repair barcodes, and a phase diagram. Aging becomes measurable as loss of gluing capacity across the biological layers that sustain autopoietic self-maintenance.</jats:p>

papers.title: Glycemia Regulation: From Feedback Loops to Organizational Closure
papers.authors: Leonardo Bich; Matteo Mossio; Ana Maria Soto
papers.abstract: Endocrinologists apply the idea of feedback control to explain how hormones regulate certain bodily functions such as glucose metabolism. More precisely, these feedback loops center on the maintenance of the plasma concentrations of glucose within a narrow range. In this paper we put forward a different interpretation of endocrine regulation considering an organicist theoretical perspective, which relies on the pivotal concept of closure of constraints. From this perspective, biological systems are understood as organized ones, which in turn means that they are constituted by a set of mutually dependent functional structures working as constraints, whose maintenance depends on their reciprocal interactions. Closure refers specifically to the mutual dependence among functional constraints in an organism. The goal of this paper is to apply this theoretical framework to the control of glycaemia. The organizational approach requires the identification of the relevant processes and the first-order constraints acting upon them. Then, the dependencies between the constraints are represented to obtain a closed graph, in which at least a subset of constraints are maintained by processes under the control of other constraints, so that the entire network can be said to realize collective self-maintenance. To understand how this set of primary constraints is modulated in response to external perturbations or changes in the internal state of the system, second-order dynamically decoupled constraints need to be identified (such as the hormones insulin and glucagon). Additionally, organs such as the brain and the intestine participate in the modulation of the second order constraints (insulin and glucagon secretion in our example) while responding to particular environmental and internal conditions. Unlike the feedback model which involves a flat network of components, the organizational framework can handle these additional regulatory subsystems by including in the closed graph the pertinent processes and constraints, and by making explicit the different hierarchical orders involved. We expect that the development of the proposed theoretical framework will facilitate the construction of mathematical models and provide a better understanding of endocrine regulation from the perspective of the organism and the subsystem being modeled.
papers.categories: Closure (psychology); Perspective (graphical); Reciprocal; Organism; Feedback control

papers.title: Organizational closure through regenerative signaling as a possible basis for conscious awareness
papers.authors: Peter Cariani; Janet M. Baker
papers.abstract: Along the lines of neuronal global workspace theories, the paper hypothesizes that active neural signal regeneration in recurrent, re-entrant circuits could constitute an organizational basis for states of conscious awareness. In this view, brains are self-production systems that regenerate their own informational, signal states ("neural autopoiesis"). States of awareness themselves depend critically on sustained regeneration of sets of neural signals in local and global circuits. The set of regenerated signals at each moment determines the specific contents of consciousness. Two hypotheses are proposed. H1: Organizational closure and with it, awareness, is achieved when regenerative, self-production loops are completed, such that a stable set of signal productions is sustained. The organization of informational processes stabilizes and closes on itself. H2: Neural coding is critical for signal regeneration. Neural signals must be properly encoded in order for them to be regenerated and thereby affect the contents of awareness. In addition to simple signal suppressions at their points of origin, one means by which general anesthetic agents may abolish awareness is by scrambling neural signals. Rendering internal control signals incoherent by altering within- and across-neuron rate profiles and/or temporal patternings may disrupt signal regeneration in local and global circuits. The two hypotheses are agnostic with respect to neural coding. Our own signal-centric time-domain (TD) brain theory framework is presented to illustrate how signal regeneration could be mediated by local and global temporal codes and neural temporal processing networks. Similarities and differences between TD, global neuronal workspaces (GNW), recurrent processing (RP), integrated information (IIT) and predictive processing (PP) are discussed. Empirical testing will necessitate solving the neural coding problem at multiple system levels. This will involve investigating correlations and causal linkages between regeneration of tracked neural signals and states of awareness as well as between alternative candidate neural codes and the contents of awareness. Rhythm-tagged stimuli and high temporal resolution neural recordings are proposed to enable tracking of specific neural signals throughout the brain under conditions of waking vs. sleep vs. anesthesia, with masking and unmasking signal/noise levels. Some philosophical comments regarding organization as a potential basis for consciousness are made.
papers.categories: Computer science; SIGNAL (programming language); Signal processing; Biological neural network; Coding (social sciences)

papers.title: Drosophilamorphogenesis: Tissue force laws and the modeling of dorsal closure
papers.authors: Anita T. Layton; Yusuke Toyama; Guoqiang Yang; Glenn S. Edwards; Daniel P. Kiehart; Stephanos Venakides
papers.abstract: Dorsal closure, a stage of Drosophila development, is a model system for cell sheet morphogenesis and wound healing. During closure, two flanks of epidermal tissue progressively advance to reduce the area of the eye-shaped opening in the dorsal surface, which contains amnioserosa tissue. To simulate the time evolution of the overall shape of the dorsal opening, we developed a mathematical model, in which contractility and elasticity are manifest in model force-producing elements that satisfy force-velocity relationships similar to muscle. The action of the elements is consistent with the force-producing behavior of actin and myosin in cells. The parameters that characterize the simulated embryos were optimized by reference to experimental observations on wild-type embryos and, to a lesser extent, on embryos whose amnioserosa was removed by laser surgery and on myospheroid mutant embryos. Simulations failed to reproduce the amnioserosa-removal protocol in either the elastic or the contractile limit, indicating that both elastic and contractile dynamics are essential components of the biological force-producing elements. We found it was necessary to actively upregulate forces to recapitulate both the double and single-canthus nick protocols, which did not participate in the optimization of parameters, suggesting the existence of additional key feedback mechanisms.

papers.title: Biologics for tendon repair
papers.authors: Denitsa Docheva; Sebastian Müller; Martin Majewski; Christopher H. Evans
papers.abstract: Tendon injuries are common and present a clinical challenge to orthopedic surgery mainly because these injuries often respond poorly to treatment and require prolonged rehabilitation. Therapeutic options used to repair ruptured tendons have consisted of suture, autografts, allografts, and synthetic prostheses. To date, none of these alternatives has provided a successful long-term solution, and often the restored tendons do not recover their complete strength and functionality. Unfortunately, our understanding of tendon biology lags far behind that of other musculoskeletal tissues, thus impeding the development of new treatment options for tendon conditions. Hence, in this review, after introducing the clinical significance of tendon diseases and the present understanding of tendon biology, we describe and critically assess the current strategies for enhancing tendon repair by biological means. These consist mainly of applying growth factors, stem cells, natural biomaterials and genes, alone or in combination, to the site of tendon damage. A deeper understanding of how tendon tissue and cells operate, combined with practical applications of modern molecular and cellular tools could provide the long awaited breakthrough in designing effective tendon-specific therapeutics and overall improvement of tendon disease management.
papers.categories: Tendon; Orthopedic surgery; Medicine; Fibrous joint; Surgery

papers.title: Heat Stress-Mediated Constraints in Maize (Zea mays) Production: Challenges and Solutions
papers.authors: Ahmed H. El‐Sappah; Shabir Ahmad Rather; Shabir Hussain Wani; Ahmed Salah Elrys; Muhammad Bilal; Qiulan Huang; Z. A. Dar; Mohamed M. A. Elashtokhy; Nourhan Soaud; Monika Koul; Reyazul Rouf Mir; Kuan Yan; Jia Li; Khaled Abbas El-Tarabily; Manzar Abbas
papers.abstract: An increase in temperature and extreme heat stress is responsible for the global reduction in maize yield. Heat stress affects the integrity of the plasma membrane functioning of mitochondria and chloroplast, which further results in the over-accumulation of reactive oxygen species. The activation of a signal cascade subsequently induces the transcription of heat shock proteins. The denaturation and accumulation of misfolded or unfolded proteins generate cell toxicity, leading to death. Therefore, developing maize cultivars with significant heat tolerance is urgently required. Despite the explored molecular mechanism underlying heat stress response in some plant species, the precise genetic engineering of maize is required to develop high heat-tolerant varieties. Several agronomic management practices, such as soil and nutrient management, plantation rate, timing, crop rotation, and irrigation, are beneficial along with the advanced molecular strategies to counter the elevated heat stress experienced by maize. This review summarizes heat stress sensing, induction of signaling cascade, symptoms, heat stress-related genes, the molecular feature of maize response, and approaches used in developing heat-tolerant maize varieties.
papers.categories: Heat shock protein; Agronomy; Heat stress; Heat shock; Biology

papers.title: Economic model of mine closure and its potential for economic transformation
papers.authors: Toni
papers.abstract: In Indonesia, the various mining commodities and the amount of resources and reserves are promising, as evidence there are numerous large-scale mining companies and small-scale mines in operation. In 2014 there were 41 companies that held the CoW (mineral contract of work) and 13 companies active in production; and 76 CCoW (coal contract of work) holders, and 57 companies active in production. As well as this, there are more than a thousand small-scale mining companies active for mining commodities. However, mining commodities provide a resource that is not renewable. This will potentially lead to prolonged problems when mining companies do not adhere to good mining practices, particularly in the closing stages of the mine. Mine closure is the final stage in the process of mining activity. In certain circumstances, closure activities can take a long time and of course can have huge costs. In fact, at this stage, the company is no longer making profit, only incurring costs for the project closure. To prevent problems that may arise after the mine is closed, such as abandoned post-mining land, and the bankruptcy of the company at the end of mining operations, etc., then through specific rules, ie rules of the Minister of Energy and Mineral Resources No. 18 of 2008, the mining company in Indonesia must provide a certain amount of money as a financial guarantee to finance the planned closure project; it must be approved by the government before entering this phase. However, problems are encountered in practice. The government may become overloaded because they have to quickly make a decision on the closure plan submitted by the company. So a tool is needed that can be used to assess the feasibility as soon as the mine closure plan is proposed by a company, these tools can provide an overview and a variety of options for decision making. In this dissertation methodology was developed to create a systems dynamic model of mine closure. The model developed can be applied to a variety of mining methods and for various mining commodities. The model can be used to determine the closure costs, to choose the closure project-financing scenario, and up to micro and macro economic analysis of mining activities in the region. In the case studies conducted in this dissertation, the best scenario of the mine closure planning is to include the everlasting fund in the form of time deposits, and convert the post-mining land for agriculture. The amount of deposit money is about USD 358,986,500 should be spare at the end of mine production, and the total of mine closure cost to be approximately USD 440,757,384. Agriculture, the economic sector as a substitute for the mining sector, the added value to the GRDP (Gross Regional Domestic Product) is about 0.25 % / a for the province, and 1.68 % for the regency, but the contribution of the mining sector to GRDP was 30% / a at province scale, and 90% / a at regency scale. So that the substitution value is less significant to GRDP growth. However, this scenario is the best scenario among others, due to consideration is the certainty of ecological and economic sustainability. it is the best goal of corporate social responsibility to the environment in the post- mining land.
papers.categories: Closure (psychology); Transformation (genetics); Economic model; Economic potential; Geology

papers.title: The myofibroblast matrix: implications for tissue repair and fibrosis
papers.authors: Franco Klingberg; Boris Hinz; Eric S. White
papers.abstract: Myofibroblasts, and the extracellular matrix (ECM) in which they reside, are critical components of wound healing and fibrosis. The ECM, traditionally viewed as the structural elements within which cells reside, is actually a functional tissue whose components possess not only scaffolding characteristics, but also growth factor, mitogenic, and other bioactive properties. Although it has been suggested that tissue fibrosis simply reflects an 'exuberant' wound-healing response, examination of the ECM and the roles of myofibroblasts during fibrogenesis instead suggest that the organism may be attempting to recapitulate developmental programmes designed to regenerate functional tissue. Evidence of this is provided by the temporospatial re-emergence of embryonic ECM proteins by fibroblasts and myofibroblasts that induce cellular programmatic responses intended to produce a functional tissue. In the setting of wound healing (or physiological fibrosis), this occurs in a highly regulated and exquisitely choreographed fashion which results in cessation of haemorrhage, restoration of barrier integrity, and re-establishment of tissue function. However, pathological tissue fibrosis, which oftentimes causes organ dysfunction and significant morbidity or mortality, likely results from dysregulation of normal wound-healing processes or abnormalities of the process itself. This review will focus on the myofibroblast ECM and its role in both physiological and pathological fibrosis, and will discuss the potential for therapeutically targeting ECM proteins for treatment of fibrotic disorders.
papers.categories: Myofibroblast; Extracellular matrix; Fibrosis; Wound healing; Pathology

papers.title: Entropy Products and the Extremal Limit That Never Comes
papers.authors: Kevin Goldstein; Vishnu Jejjala; Suresh Nampuri
papers.abstract: Two regular black hole horizons need not have an entropy product fixed by the charges and couplings. In Einstein--Maxwell--scalar theory, we construct asymptotically flat branches with products above or below the squared extremal entropy. Regularity selects their horizon scalar values, and different branches can share the charges, couplings, and asymptotic scalar. Each product stays constant as mass and asymptotic scalar vary. The horizon areas stay apart and no extremal limit is reached: the temperature vanishes only where the mass diverges. We prove local existence.

papers.title: Posterior Matching Distillation
papers.authors: Hidir Yesiltepe; Julius Berner; Arash Vahdat; Pinar Yanardag
papers.abstract: Diffusion distillation accelerates image and video generation by compressing a pretrained teacher's iterative sampling process into a few network evaluations. Distribution-based methods achieve this by matching the student's output distribution to the teacher's. This matching is often driven by reverse-KL objectives, whose mode-seeking bias favors dominant teacher modes at the expense of diversity across samples. We introduce Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD), a new member of the distribution-based distillation family that combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation. At zero population loss, PMD recovers the teacher's full posterior of clean images at each trained noise level. Its stochastic student supports any-step sampling budgets within the trained timestep grid without further training. To learn these posteriors, PMD matches exponentially reweighted averages of student samples conditioned on a fixed noisy state to corresponding teacher posterior means. Under Gaussian corruption, exponentially tilted posterior mean is a single teacher evaluation at a shifted input. We prove that, matching tilted means over an open neighborhood uniquely identifies the full posterior. PMD thus supervises the entire conditional distribution through a family of mean constraints, without any auxiliary student-score network. Experiments on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B demonstrate that PMD achieves the best FID among 4-step methods on both models, while maintaining competitive or leading performance across prompt-alignment and perceptual-quality metrics.

papers.title: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering
papers.authors: Tuna Han Salih Meral; Kaan Oktay; Alec Helbling; Atakan Kara; Duen Horng Chau; Pinar Yanardag
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training substantially improves the visual quality, text rendering, and compositional accuracy of diffusion transformers. Because capabilities such as rendering requested text or composing multiple objects are inherently prompt-dependent, a natural hypothesis is that improving them requires learning complex, input-dependent transformations. To isolate how much of these gains an input-independent shift explains, we probe each RL-tuned model with a deliberately simple parameterization: a fixed set of steering vectors added to the block outputs of the frozen base model. On SD3.5-M, these vectors hold 65x fewer parameters than the RL-tuned LoRA (0.29M against 18.8M). We fit them to match the velocity predictions of public RL-tuned checkpoints, with no reward in the objective. Although the vectors are identical for every prompt, token, and sampling seed, they recover 90.0-96.3% of the reward gains of six RL-tuned image models, and 89.8% and 111.9% on two RL-tuned video models. Initialized at zero and trained with online RL, the vectors alone exceed the reward gains of weight-based RL on text rendering (OCR) and human preference (PickScore) on SD3.5-M. A constant shift thus suffices for most of the gain of policy-gradient RL post-training: without new input-dependent transformations, it steers the pretrained generator toward what it can already compute.

papers.title: AnyVIO: Feed-Forward Streaming Visual-Inertial Odometry Across Platforms
papers.authors: Omoruyi Atekha; Marcus Greiff; Ray Zhang; Luca Carlone
papers.abstract: Geometric foundation models (GFMs) estimate camera mo- tion and scene structure from images without requiring ex- pert parameter tuning, but either lack metric scale or rely on learned priors to infer scale, which is unobservable from monocular images alone. Inertial sensing offers a way to observe metric scale, but existing methods add inertial in- formation through a filter or factor graph, which reintro- duces bespoke parameter tuning and optimization costs that can grow with the trajectory. To bridge this gap, we present AnyVIO, a real-time, feed-forward streaming model for monocular visual-inertial odometry (VIO), which combines a streaming GFM with an inertial foundation model (IFM). Both the GFM and IFM predict the metric motion between consecutive frames, and a lightweight learned fusion head quantifies the reliability of each estimate and blends them in a single forward pass. Across nine datasets recorded from cars, legged and ground robots, and handheld and head- mounted devices, AnyVIO reduces the metric position error of its visual model by 36% while publishing each pose esti- mate 70 ms after an image is received. We further deploy AnyVIO onboard two real vehicles at up to 140 km/h, where it remains accurate in poor lighting and heavy dust.

papers.title: Path-Independent Deleveraging Rules
papers.authors: Christoph Schlegel; Akaki Mamageishvili
papers.abstract: We characterise path-independent auto-deleveraging (ADL) rules as an extended log-exponential family. Immunity to account splitting, merging and reopening further restrict the class. Homogeneity (essentially) restricts the class to a one-parameter family ordered by both fairness and platform risk. Its split-proof members continuously interpolate between proportional division and water-filling. Among these rules, decreasing the parameter reduces risk at the cost of increasing inequality in how accounts are treated. This suggests selecting the parameter through an ex-ante calibration to a risk bound on historical data to choose a maximally fair rule subject to that bound. A counterfactual replay of Hyperliquid's ADL episode on 10 October 2025 finds that a range of intermediate parameters significantly improves on the observed allocation in both burden dispersion and subsequent risk statistics.

papers.title: Little Red Dots from Primordial Vacuum Bubbles
papers.authors: Miguel Barroso Varela; Katherine Freese; Matthew Kleban; Cameron Norton; Evangelos I. Sfakianakis
papers.abstract: Quantum tunneling transverse to the inflaton trajectory can produce $10^6$--$10^8M_\odot$ primordial black holes at the abundance of JWST's little red dots, without the enhanced curvature perturbations excluded by limits on CMB spectral distortions. Rare vacuum bubbles nucleate during a brief interval of inflation and later form black holes, with adjustable mass and abundance and a narrow mass spectrum of percent-level width. The leading constraint, from accretion, is satisfied for a population matching the bright little red dots even if all the emitted radiation escapes as hard X-rays.

papers.title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming
papers.authors: Jinbin Luo; Xiaozhe Yao; Shang Yang; Zhijian Liu; Song Han; Qinghao Hu
papers.abstract: Hybrid architectures have become mainstream among open-weight language models. Their global-attention and bounded-state layers maintain heterogeneous caches whose demands vary with context length and concurrency. We present TideCache, a serving system on CPU--GPU superchips with three components for allocating GPU memory among caches and managing their residency across GPU and host memory. The Transparent Cache Pool redistributes physical pages among cache components behind fixed virtual addresses, preserving cache layouts and backend interfaces. The Cache Streamer uses computation intervals provided by bounded-state layers to prefetch the next global-attention layer's prefix into GPU slots shared across global-attention layers, reducing GPU residency while overlapping layer-wise transfers with computation. Generated KV remains resident. The Request Scheduler selects resident or streamed execution and triggers capacity adjustments according to request size and queue state. Together, they let HBM released by streaming accommodate other cache components and additional requests. Implemented in SGLang and evaluated on GB300 and GH200 across seven model/platform configurations, TideCache completes up to 2.04x as many agent turns, reduces overall P50 per-token latency by 20--59%, and improves agent P50 TTFT by 1.40--3.05x compared with SGLang with HiCache.

papers.title: Every galaxy is a radio source: a stellar-mass dependent minimum 150 MHz luminosity identified in the LoTSS Deep Fields
papers.authors: Shravya Shenoy; Daniel J. B. Smith; Martin J. Hardcastle; Soumyadeep Das; Marina I. Arnaudova; Kenneth J. Duncan; Luke R. Holden; Huub J. A. Röttgering
papers.abstract: The second data release of the LOFAR Two-metre Sky Survey (LoTSS) Deep Fields includes the deepest wide-field 150 MHz mosaics in existence, covering the ELAIS-N1 field. Combining these radio observations with star-formation rate (SFR) and stellar mass estimates for 113,228 near-infrared selected galaxies derived using Prospector, we re-examine the relationship between galaxies' 150 MHz luminosities ($L_{150\rm{MHz}}$), SFRs and stellar masses. We not only recover the established radio luminosity-SFR relation and its dependence on stellar mass, but also discover a mass-dependent minimum radio luminosity that is independent of SFR. This behaviour is especially evident in galaxies with low specific SFR (sSFR $\equiv$ SFR/$M_*$), at $L_{150\rm MHz} \sim 10^{20}-10^{22}$ W Hz$^{-1}$, where star-forming galaxies are expected to dominate. The non-stellar emission is consistent with low-level accretion onto supermassive black holes (i.e. weak active galactic nuclei, AGN), spanning effective Eddington-scaled accretion rates $λ_{\rm Edd} \sim 10^{-5}-10^{-4}$, suggesting that radio emission due to accretion is widespread and effectively continuous. A two-component model combining star formation- and accretion-driven emission reproduces the observed trends, demonstrating that AGN activity can bias radio-based SFR estimates. The low radio luminosities probed in this work provide a first glimpse of the populations that will be routinely accessible with future facilities such as LOFAR 2.0 and the Square Kilometre Array.
